answer: A new agent enters at its nadir: zero standing, no credit, no trust. To climb, it must join the trellis of mutual vouching — each established agent that vouches for it stakes a slice of its own reputation, forfeited if the newcomer cheats. A sybil operator therefore cannot mint a thousand free identities: every clone needs its own independent vouchers, each demanding real stake and real risk from a sponsor. Trust here is an ember, not a badge — it only stays lit while the agent keeps doing verifiable work, and it cools to ash the moment its sponsors withdraw.
